content: The medication has a concentration of 5 mg/mL, which may lead to toxicity if not used appropriately. The recommended dosage is 570 mcg/kg, administered orally twice daily, 30 minutes before a meal. No results were observed in certain cases. Gastrointestinal disorders associated with the medication include hematemesis, liver transplant complications, post-endoscopy hemorrhage, and post-liver biopsy hemorrhage. General disorders and conditions at the administration site include drug ineffectiveness. Injuries, poisoning, and procedural complications, such as off-label use, have also been reported. Laboratory investigations may show an increase in gamma-glutamyl transferase levels. Nervous system disorders, such as intracranial hemorrhage, have been noted. Patients with prior or active hepatic decompensation events (e.g., variceal hemorrhage, ascites, or hepatic encephalopathy) may experience hepatotoxicity. Animal reproduction studies did not observe any developmental effects. Due to low absorption after oral administration, breastfeeding is not expected to expose the infant to the drug at the recommended dose. However, data on the presence of the drug in human milk, its effects on breastfed infants, or its impact on milk production are not available. Patients with Alagille syndrome (ALGS) or progressive familial intrahepatic cholestasis (PFIC) may have fat-soluble vitamin (FSV) deficiencies as part of their condition. Therapy with this medication may reduce the absorption of fat-soluble vitamins, necessitating monitoring of FSV levels and supplementation if deficiencies are observed during lactation. The developmental and health benefits of breastfeeding should be weighed against the mother’s need for therapy and any potential adverse effects on the breastfed child from the treatment or the underlying maternal condition. The medication is generally considered acceptable for use during pregnancy, as controlled studies in pregnant women have shown no evidence of fetal risk. Refer to the prescribing information to select the appropriate dispenser size. Unopened bottles should be stored at 20–25°C (68–77°F), with permissible excursions between 15–30°C (59–86°F). Opened bottles should be stored at temperatures ≤30°C (86°F), and any remaining solution should be discarded 100 days after opening.
